newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriots to discourage visits to Turkish side.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriots to discourage visits to Turkish side.

text.p: Greek Cypriots will discourage visits to the Turkish held areas of the island for the second consecutive weekend by demonstrating against the division of Cyprus at a U.N. checkpoint, organisers said on Friday.
"(Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf) Denktash is going to feel even poorer this week," Greek Cypriot member of parliament Marios Matsakis, who is spearheading the campaign, told Reuters.

Groups of Greek Cypriots gathered at the United Nations-controlled Ledra Palace checkpoint in the capital Nicosia last weekend and blocked the road to the Turkish-held north, usually used by tourists and diplomats.

By discouraging visits to the north organisers are attempting to put economic pressure on the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state created in 1983 and recognised only by Ankara. Greek Cypriots are not allowed visits.
The demonstration has not been sanctioned by the government.
"We want the right message to be put across, but there should be care to avoid harassment," one official source said.
Organisers say they are not forcibly stopping tourists, but informing them of the situation on the island. "We will be there this weekend and every weekend," Matsakis said.
Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 in the wake of a short-lived coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time.
Efforts under United Nations auspices to reunite the island as a bicommunal bizonal federation have so far been unsuccessful.
